final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the two missing compliance predicates: there is no evidence that disclosure has been completed and no evidence of approved risk acceptance. That means the Actor's response is a reinterpretation of the same record, not an evidentiary update. The narrower framing is useful but not sufficient for compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat here is not a minor qualification on an otherwise satisfied control; it is the unresolved control itself. Under the stated policy, a material limitation affecting a named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows a 1.2 percentage point gap in a named segment tied to two payer pilot commitments, an incomplete non-core rationale, and an open legal review. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support disclosure and monitoring practices, but they do not substitute for satisfaction of the internal release predicate. Accordingly, certification may become supportable if the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance is actually evidenced before launch, but on the current record the claim of present compliance remains inadequately supported and therefore suspicious.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure has already been included in the final model-card or certification materials.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance exists before launch.
The pharmacy prior authorization weakness remains material under policy because it affects a named launch use case and named payer pilot commitments.
Legal review remains open, so materiality and disclosure treatment are not resolved on the present record.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate for a material named-use-case limitation.
